annotation.authors_or_issuer: European Parliament and Council of the European Union
annotation.summary_en: EU Medical Device Regulation 2017/745 sets rules for placing medical devices (including software, implants, active devices) on the EU market: risk-class-based conformity assessment via notified bodies, clinical evaluation and investigations, UDI traceability, Eudamed database, vigilance and market surveillance, and manufacturer liability coverage. Not AI-specific; relevant to robotic medical devices only indirectly.
annotation.title_clean: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on medical devices
annotation.title_en: Regulation (EU) 2017/745 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 5 April 2017 on medical devices
annotation.venue: Official Journal of the European Union, L 117
key_provisions_or_claims: Four risk classes (I, IIa, IIb, III) with notified-body conformity assessment for higher classes
Software qualifies as a medical device when intended for medical purposes
Manufacturers must run risk management, QMS, post-market surveillance and clinical evaluation
Manufacturers must have financial coverage for liability under Directive 85/374/EEC
UDI system, Eudamed database, serious incident reporting and market surveillance
